label: copy-phase input k while outputting q (or a), late in recall
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (never during original input or the delimiter), almost always at recall_idx >= 3. 88% of activation mass is on steps where the fed-back input is k, and about 12% on input q (mainly a q that comes right after k, as in k q q, at low magnitude). Magnitude depends mostly on the token being output: input k with output q gives the strongest activations (top examples ~0.9-1.0 of max, all the bigram k->q in the original); k->a is next. Other k->x transitions activate weakly or not at all. The feature is sparse even inside its niche: only ~4% of copy-phase k inputs activate, k->q at recall_idx>=3 has ~86% precision but covers only ~57% of mass. Does not fire on k at early recall positions (recall_idx 0-2), on other letters or digits, or on any first occurrence of a token.

scorecard.summary: Weighted combination of 40 cues.
